questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question assesses practical knowledge of traffic management in multi-tenant environments. It tests understanding of Istio's traffic splitting capabilities, header-based routing, and safe rollout strategies. Candidates must balance per-tenant isolation against system complexity.

## Key Concepts

- **Istio traffic management**: DestinationRules define service subsets; VirtualServices handle routing rules
- **Canary deployments**: Gradually shift traffic between versions to validate changes safely
- **Header-based routing**: Use x-cluster-local headers or custom headers like X-TENANT-ID to identify tenants
- **Weight-based traffic splitting**: Distribute traffic percentages across subsets

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: DestinationRule
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway-dr
spec:
  host: cnf-gateway
  subsets:
  - name: prod
    labels:
      version: prod
  - name: canary
    labels:
      version: canary
---
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway-vs
spec:
  hosts:
  - cnf-gateway
  http:
  - match:
    - headers:
        x-tenant-id:
          exact: canary
    route:
    - destination:
        host: cnf-gateway
        subset: canary
      weight: 15
    - destination:
        host: cnf-gateway
        subset: prod
      weight: 85
  - route:
    - destination:
        host: cnf-gateway
        subset: prod
```

## One-Namespace Test Validation

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: canary-test
  labels:
    istio-injection: enabled
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway-prod
  namespace: canary-test
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cnf-gateway
      version: prod
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cnf-gateway
        version: prod
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: cnf-gateway:v1
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: canary-test
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 8080
  selector:
    app: cnf-gateway
```

Validate with: `curl -H "X-TENANT-ID: canary" http://cnf-gateway/` to confirm routing behavior.

## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical understanding of per-tenant TLS in CNF gateways, including CSR workflows, in-cluster signing, and secure TLS termination at the gateway. Emphasizes using Kubernetes Secrets for certificates and small manifests for end-to-end validation.

## Key Concepts

- mTLS in CNF gateways
- per-tenant CA and secret management
- CSR signing in-cluster
- sidecar certificate injection

## Code Example

```yaml
# TenantCredential secret (example)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tenant1-credential
type: kubernetes.io/tls
data:
  tls.crt: <base64-cert>
  tls.key: <base64-key>

# Per-tenant CA bundle secret
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tenant1-ca
type: Opaque
data:
  ca.crt: <base64-ca>

# One-namespace test manifest
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gw-tenant1
  namespace: tenant1
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: cnf/gateway:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 443
        volumeMounts:
        - name: ca-volume
          mountPath: /etc/ssl/certs
      - name: sidecar-mtls
        image: cnf/sidecar-mtls:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: ca-volume
          mountPath: /etc/tenant-ca
      volumes:
      - name: ca-volume
        secret:
          secretName: tenant1-ca
```

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests the ability to design tenant-isolated API validation using per-tenant OpenAPI specs, driven by a request header, within a CNF gateway. It emphasizes practical config storage, request validation, error handling, and observability.

## Key Concepts

- Per-tenant OpenAPI specs stored in ConfigMaps
- Tenant selection via X-TENANT-ID header
- Lightweight JSON validation using Ajv or similar
- Structured error responses (400) with detailed validation messages
- Audit logging for security and debugging
- Namespace-scoped manifests for isolation

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudo-validator flow:
// 1. Extract X-TENANT-ID header from request
// 2. Load corresponding OpenAPI spec from cnf.api.spec ConfigMap
// 3. Compile Ajv validator from spec
// 4. Validate request body and headers against schema
// 5. Return 400 with structured error if validation fails
// 6. Pass through to upstream service if valid
```

## Minimal YAML

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf.api.spec
data:
  tenant-a.yaml: |-
    openapi: 3.0.0
    paths:
      /api/resource:
        post:
          requestBody:
            required: true
            content:
              application/json:
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example
```yaml
# Tenant CRD (simplified)
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: tenants.cnf.example.com
spec:
  group: cnf.example.com
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              tenantID: { type: string }
              namespace: { type: string }
              desiredVersion: { type: string }
  scope: Cluster
  names:
    plural: tenants
    singular: tenant
    kind: Tenant
    shortNames: [ tns ]
```

```yaml
# Tenant canary Deployment (tenant-a)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cnf-gateway
        tenant: tenant-a
        version: v2
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: registry.example/cnf/gateway:v2
```

```yaml
# Istio TrafficSplit example for canary (tenant-a)
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  http:
  - route:
    - destination:
        host: cnf-gateway.tenant-a.svc.cluster.local
        subset: v1
      weight: 90
    - destination:
        host: cnf-gateway.tenant-a.svc.cluster.local
        subset: v2
      weight: 10
```
